steps.message: Git reports the tree but the project dir is ignored by the parent repo, so let me show the changed regions directly:

The build passes. Here's what I found and fixed.

## Root cause

In `ManageFishingSpotFragment.verifyUserInput()`, the fishing spot's coordinates were read from the **center of the map camera**, completely ignoring the latitude/longitude `InputTextView` widgets:

```java
fishingSpot.setLatitude(mMap.getCameraPosition().target.latitude);
fishingSpot.setLongitude(mMap.getCameraPosition().target.longitude);
```

The only path from the text fields back to the map was the "sync" (refresh) button's click listener. So typing coordinates and saving without pressing sync discarded the typed values and persisted whatever the map happened to be centered on.

## Changes to `ManageFishingSpotFragment.java`

1. **`verifyUserInput()` now reads and validates coordinates from the text views** (`getCoordinateInput`) and shows an `AlertUtils.showError(...)` dialog with the existing `msg_invalid_coordinate` string if either value is empty, unparseable, or out of range. The name/duplicate-name checks stay ahead of it so existing error precedence is unchanged.

2. **Replaced `validateCoordinateInput()` with `getCoordinateInput()`**, which returns a nullable `Double` instead of a `-1` sentinel. The old sentinel was itself a latent bug: `-1` is a perfectly legal coordinate, so a user entering latitude `-1` had their input silently rejected by the sync button. It also null-guards `getInputText()` (which returns `null` for empty input, so the old code would have thrown an NPE on `inputText.length()`), and still handles the `,`-as-decimal-separator locale case plus partial input like `-` or `.`.

3. **Added `isValidCoordinates(double, double)`** which range-checks the **raw doubles**. I deliberately did not reuse `DraggableMapFragment.isValid(LatLng)` here: `LatLng`'s constructor clamps latitude to ±90 and wraps longitude into ±180, so out-of-range input becomes valid by the time that check runs. Checking before constructing the `LatLng` makes the validation actually effective.

4. **`updateViews()` now populates the coordinate views from the spot being edited** before touching the map. `updateMap()` bails out early when `mMap == null` (e.g. Google Play Services unavailable), which previously left the fields at the `0.000000` default; now that coordinates are sourced from those fields, that would have silently zeroed out an existing spot's location on save.

The sync button is preserved and still works — it now shares the same parse/validate helpers, so its behavior is consistent with saving.

One behavioral note worth flagging: the old per-keystroke-style feedback (`Utils.showToast` + `input.pressBackspace()`) was wired only into the sync button, where auto-deleting a character on click was odd. The sync button now shows the toast without mutating the user's text. `InputTextView.pressBackspace()` is consequently unused, but I left the public method in place rather than widening the patch.
